name: POST /api/leadflow/authz/evaluate - batched policy decisions for a screen
description: Ask the policy decision point whether the signed-in caller may take each of a set of actions, and get one verdict per action in a single round trip. BATCHED BY DESIGN: a screen like the Capture Inbox decides whether to render a Route button, a Reassign control, a bulk export and an override, and asking separately would be four calls before the first paint, growing with every control added. The request carries an `actions` array and the response carries a `decisions` array in the SAME ORDER, so a caller can zip them positionally without matching on strings. An empty actions array is a 400 rather than an empty success: asking nothing is a caller bug, and answering it cheerfully hides the bug until a screen silently renders no controls. The array is capped at 50 - beyond that the screen is asking the wrong question. EFFECT is `permit`, `deny`, or `requires_approval`, and that third value is the point of this endpoint. SOP §28 does not say a Rep may never change offer terms; it says a Rep may not do it WITHOUT APPROVAL. Collapsing that into deny would delete the escalation path the business runs on, so the UI can use it to show a 'request approval' affordance instead of hiding the control. OBLIGATIONS are conditions attached to a permit that the caller MUST honour - for example a second-party approval reference, or an audit purpose that has to be supplied with the write. They are returned as a list per decision, and a permit carrying an unmet obligation is not a permit. DECISION REFERENCE: every verdict carries decision_ref, a stable id the caller quotes on the subsequent mutating call so the write and the authorisation that allowed it can be joined afterwards - which is what makes an audit answerable rather than a guess. Protected by the authenticate guard; the Authorization header is required. QA: depends on register and login, and needs no other fixture because it evaluates against the caller's own roles rather than a stored resource.

testCases.name: Evaluate a screen's action set in one call
Reject an empty action set rather than answering nothing
Reject an action outside the permission vocabulary
Reject a batch larger than the cap
Reject a bearer token that fails verification

errorCases.message: actions must be a non-empty array of at most 50 known actions
errorCases.when: actions is absent, empty, larger than 50, or contains an action outside the permission vocabulary or an entry with no resource_type

errorCases.message: Authorization header with a bearer token is required
errorCases.when: the Authorization header is absent, or present without a Bearer token

errorCases.message: Session token is invalid or expired
errorCases.when: the bearer token fails verification or has expired
